chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Ibn Muskan, from Al-Halbi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding His Mighty and Majestic saying: 'Give them a deed of manumission if you know any good in them.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'If you know that they have wealth and religion (piety).'

key_terms.خَيْراً: Good (interpreted here as wealth and piety)
key_terms.فَكَاتِبُوهُمْ: Give them a deed of manumission/contract

ai.seo_question: What does 'good' mean in the Quranic verse about slave manumission according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) interprets the term 'good' (khayran) in Surah An-Nur (24:33) as requiring both financial capability (mal) and religious piety (din), ensuring the slave can fulfill the contract faithfully. This dual criterion reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on integrating material competence with spiritual integrity in legal transactions, preventing exploitation while promoting the slave's moral and economic independence.
